Find ${lim}_{x\to \,-1}(5+7x)^{3}(f(x)-x)^{4}$ for the function $f(x)$ plotted above.
question.worked_solution:
From the graph, we get that ${lim}_{x\to \,-1}f(x)=0.$ 

From the product rule, we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,-1}(5+7x)^{3}(f(x)-x)^{4}={lim}_{x\to \,-1}(5+7x)^{3}\cdot {lim}_{x\to \,-1}(f(x)-x)^{4}.
$$

We calculate the limits of each factor, separately.

Applying the power rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,-1}(5+7x)^{3} & ={({lim}_{x\to \,-1}(5+7x))}^{3} \\  & =(5+7\cdot (-1))^{3} \\  & =(-2)^{3} \\  & =-8,\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,-1}(f(x)-x)^{4} & ={({lim}_{x\to \,-1}(f(x)-x))}^{4} \\  & =(0-(-1))^{4} \\  & ={1}^{4} \\  & =1\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,-1}(5+7x)^{3}(f(x)-x)^{4} & ={lim}_{x\to \,-1}(5+7x)^{3}\cdot {lim}_{x\to \,-1}(f(x)-x)^{4} \\  & =(-8)\cdot (1) \\  & =-8\,.\end{aligned}
$$
